title: Support transforming oklab/oklch functions with variables in alpha value
impact: 3 reactions, one +1-style comment. Pattern comes from Tailwind v3 opacity utilities (`/ var(--tw-text-opacity)`) with a custom oklch palette; Tailwind v4 uses color-mix() instead, and oklch/lab are supported in all major browsers since 2023 (Chrome 111, Safari 15.4, Firefox 113), so only users targeting older browsers are affected. Maintainer (2023) said it 'could probably be done' and invited a contribution.
summary: oklch()/oklab()/lab()/lch() (and color()) with a var() alpha are passed through unchanged even for targets without support, so old browsers get no usable color. rgb()/hsl() with a var() alpha are already handled by UnresolvedColor; the request is to extend it to the other color functions with an sRGB fallback plus @supports-guarded p3/lab versions, as is already done for fully-resolved colors inside custom properties and var()-containing declarations.
repro: 592-repro.mjs. `.a{color:oklch(92.19% 0.04 20 / var(--o))}` with targets chrome 90 / safari 14 -> `.a{color:oklch(92.19% .04 20 / var(--o))}` (no fallback) on local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1. Same for oklab and lab. For comparison, `color: oklch(92.19% 0.04 20) var(--y)` already gets `#ffdbda var(--y)` + @supports p3/lab blocks.
evidence: repro.mjs on local master and latest 3 releases; controls (modern targets unchanged, var() in components passes through, rgb var-alpha lowered to rgba()) pass.

fix.approach: Add UnresolvedColor variants for lab/lch/oklab/oklch/color() holding the resolved components and an unresolved alpha TokenList; make TokenList::get_necessary_fallbacks/get_fallback handle them by converting the components (rgb/p3/lab) and keeping the alpha tokens, so the existing @supports fallback emission applies. var() in the color components (comment by mattpilott) cannot be lowered statically and stays out of scope. JS AST: new union cases on UnresolvedColor (additive).

notVerified: Did not browser-check a hand-written expected output; no output exists yet to compare.
